summary: Backend-only iteration 6: verified the registration bug fix for myscraptv@gmail.com. Pre-check confirmed the leftover test account was deleted from MongoDB (NOT FOUND). New test file test_registration_verify.py (4 tests) verified: (1) POST /api/auth/register with myscraptv@gmail.com/TmpVerify123 returns 200 with access_token and user.is_admin=true (SUPER_ADMIN auto-grant) — NOT the previous 409 auth.email_unavailable; (2) POST /api/auth/login works and returns is_admin=true; (3) GET /api/auth/me with the bearer token returns the profile (email + is_admin=true); (4) a duplicate register correctly returns 409 auth.email_unavailable — proving the original bug was the leftover test account. First full-suite run exposed a test-isolation issue in MY OWN new test file (left the account registered, causing 2 failures + 4 skips in the super-admin module); fixed by adding a module-scoped autouse fixture that deletes the account from Mongo before AND after the module — not an app bug. Final regression: 80/80 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed. MANDATORY CLEANUP DONE: db.users.deleteMany({email:'myscraptv@gmail.com'}) deleted 1 doc (recreated by the regression suite's super-admin fixture), post-delete Mongo find_one returns NOT FOUND, and public API login for that email now returns 401 — the real user can register fresh with their own password.
